Subject: Sourcing playbook: hosted vs dedicated vs private — procurement readiness

Hi Maya / David —

Great to sync earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has what they need to evaluate vendor pathing.

Call highlights (short):
- Primary need: production-grade inference for our patient triage assistant (low latency, HIPAA adjacency)
- Data residency: US-only; SOC 2 Type II evidence required
- Purchasing preference: finance prefers PO for enterprise deals, but they are open to marketplace if it simplifies billing
- Typical timeline: 4–6 weeks from RFP checklist receipt to PO issuance (per your note)

Key procurement questions for Novus we flagged:
1) Preferred purchase path: PO + invoice, or credit card/marketplace purchase?
2) Is a reserved capacity (monthly commit) acceptable versus on-demand usage? Any internal commit thresholds?
3) Who is the procurement contact and what is your purchasing approval workflow (legal review, finance, IT security)?

What I’m attaching: a preliminary two-path quote (hosted on-demand vs 12‑month reserved Dedicated) and a short SOW draft so your procurement/legal teams can see terms and scope. Attach: Redwood_Quote_Novus_20270912.pdf, SOW_Redwood_Novus_v1.docx

Proposed next step: commercial alignment call next week with Procurement + Finance + Redwood (30 min) to confirm PO process and commitment appetite. I’m available Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Sourcing playbook: hosted vs dedicated vs private — procurement readiness

Ben — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick answers from our side: 

- Purchasing path: our standard is PO + net 30 invoice. Finance will push for PO unless there is a strong reason to use AWS Marketplace billing.
- Procurement contact: procurement@novushealth.com (they handle intake and vendor docs).
- Timeline: for an SOW + pricing in this range, plan for a 4–6 week window for approvals (legal + security + finance).
- Commit appetite: clinical ops prefers predictable monthly commits for latency guarantees, but procurement will need the business case for a 12‑month commit vs on-demand. We may pilot on-demand for first quarter and then move to reserved capacity if ops is satisfied.

Security/compliance notes: we require SOC 2 Type II report (or SSAE equivalent) and an affirmation of US-only processing for PHI-adjacent telemetry.

I’ve attached our procurement intake checklist (Novus_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx) to this reply for your intake team.

—Maya

Subject: Re: Sourcing playbook: hosted vs dedicated vs private — procurement readiness

Thanks Maya — very helpful. Taking that into account, here’s a short commercial playbook for procurement to review (high level):

1) Hosted (Redwood API - on‑demand):
- Billing: usage-based per-token and per-embedding; minimal upfront; fast time-to-value for pilots
- Pros: no long-term commitment, low procurement friction (credit card or marketplace possible)
- Cons: higher unit cost under sustained load, less predictable monthly spend

2) Dedicated (Reserved capacity):
- Billing: committed monthly capacity (12-month or 24-month term options) with blended per-token pricing
- Pros: predictable cost and latency SLAs; preferred by engineering for consistent throughput
- Cons: requires procurement/finance commit approval; cancellation terms in contract

3) Private (VPC / on‑prem package):
- Billing: license + support + optional managed service fees; tailored to compliance/regulatory needs
- Pros: full isolation, supports strict data residency and HSM/KMS integration
- Cons: longest procurement/legal cycle; higher TCO up-front

Recommended next steps:
- Marissa (Legal/Commercial) and I can prepare a two-column one-pager comparing PO + Marketplace billing, scoped for Novus (cost delta estimates included).
- If you want to pilot quickly, we can enable a 30-day on-demand PoC account; if Novus is comfortable with reserved pricing after pilot, we’ll convert to a Dedicated commit.

Would Tue 9/14 10am PT or Wed 9/15 9am PT work for a 30-min procurement alignment? I’ll send a calendar invite with the quote and SOW attached.

Attached: Redwood_Quote_Novus_20270912.pdf, SOW_Redwood_Novus_v1.docx

Best,
Ben
